Jordan (Eng-API): quick check — proposing proto-first for a bunch of internal svc boundaries. main selling point: typed contracts + generator safety. downside: gateway needs to transcode for browser clients and some legacy callers. worried about losing quota/route telemetry when gateway reshapes requests. anyone run into this?
Maya (Platform): we did a mini spike — gateway translation ended up dropping some tenant headers unless we explicitly wired them through. ugly but fixable. the bigger issue was sampling/latency histograms getting aggregated at gateway instead of backend.
Omar (Eng-Platform): +1. gateway-level aggregation messes up per-model routing signals we use in console. if the gateway reports p50/p95, it masks backend variance that matters for rollouts.
Liz (DevEx): from DX: proto-first helps SDK ergonomics a lot. but customers expect the console to show accurate per-route cost/latency. if gateway collapses routes telemetry, it's confusing. any ideas for preserving fidelity?
Aditya (SRE): we pushed a tiny header-preserve shim in one org: add X-Original-Route + X-Orig-Latency-ms and let backend forward. worked for quotas but we had to ensure sampling IDs were stable. also watch trace-id propagation.
Jordan (Eng-API): interesting. so options seem: 1) gateway passthrough (no translation) 2) gateway translate but propagate enriched headers 3) lightweight gateway + sidecar per-service for translation/telemetry. tradeoffs?
Maya (Platform): 1) keeps telemetry clean but breaks browser clients unless we have a JSON facade. 2) is pragmatic: gateway does translation but attaches metadata for telemetry & quota calculation downstream. need a stable schema for the metadata.
Omar (Eng-Platform): 3) more infra but gives best fidelity. sidecar can emit per-method metrics and handle proto<->json near the service boundary. downside: rollout complexity and more runtime components.
Liz (DevEx): UX ask: whatever we pick, console should let non-engineers see both "edge view" and "backend view" metrics. e.g., gateway-level requests vs service-method-level requests. otherwise A/B rollout dashboards mislead PMs.
Jordan (Eng-API): proposal draft: adopt proto-first for contracts, implement gateway translation with a required telemetry envelope header: `X-RW-Telemetry: {"route":"svc.foo.Get", "method":"Get", "orig_path":"/v1/foo"}`. backends must parse and emit metrics using that envelope if present. fallback: use trace-based heuristics. thoughts?
Aditya (SRE): avoid encoding JSON in headers; header size and parsing overhead. prefer compact base64 protobuf for telemetry envelope: `X-RW-Telemetry-B64`. also need a version field for evolution.
Maya (Platform): +1 to versioned binary envelope. add validation at gateway so malformed header is dropped with a log and metric. we also need a migration plan for services that don't honor the envelope yet.
Omar (Eng-Platform): can we leverage our existing quota service? if gateway forwards the envelope, quota checks can still be gateway-side but we should emit both gateway and backend quota-consumption events.
Liz (DevEx): for rollout UX: add a toggle in console to "show backend metrics" that queries the telemetry store with `envelope.route` tag. default still shows gateway-level SLOs so customers aren't confused.
Jordan (Eng-API): I'll sketch an RFC. short-term action items: Jordan/Omar add telemetry-envelope proto + base64 header spec; Aditya give parsing/size limits for SRE; Maya wire validation behavior; Liz design console toggle mockups.
Aditya (SRE): FYI deploy-bot just pushed a canary of gateway v2 to prod-2 — it has header passthrough mode. watch for `gateway.telemetry.envelope.missing` metric.
deploy-bot: canary deployed gateway-v2 to prod-2 at 2024-11-07T14:27:30Z :rocket:
Maya (Platform): noted. let's sync tomorrow 10am PT to review RFC and console mocks.
Jordan (Eng-API): thanks all. saving notes to the RFC draft in #eng-platform-rfcs.
